A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same personalized invariant representation approach. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and methods, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original MRI and PET/CT generation and segmentation experiments, component ablations, and cross-dataset transfer results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds baseline results, an input-volume comparison, and representation visualizations.

M1.justification: The SwinUNETR backbone, learnable prior, attention/fusion mechanism, pre-training losses, and downstream task-plus-invariance objective remain unchanged, as do Algorithms 1–2. Naming the approach PUIR and explicitly organizing it into two stages do not introduce a new procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the reported BRATS23 MRI transfer, BRATS18 missing-modality segmentation, AutoPET-II PET/CT experiments, and HNSCC-to-NSCLC transfer scenario. The larger input volume and added comparators do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands SSL comparisons: SwinUNETR pre-training joins the BRATS18 comparison, while SwinMM, PCRL v2, and VoCo join AutoPET segmentation. Conversely, UNETR's AutoPET segmentation results and GcGAN/CUT's T2-to-FLAIR entries disappear. MS-SPADE's transfer comparisons remain available elsewhere.

E3.justification: v3 Table 2 adds a 192×192×192 input configuration alongside the retained 96×96×96 setting. Added SSL comparisons specify matched datasets and, for BRATS18 SwinUNETR pre-training, matched epochs, learning rates, and other hyperparameters. Existing splits and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds focused t-SNE analyses of patient embeddings on BRATS23 (Figure 5) and PET/CT alignment under different constraints (Figure 9), plus an input-volume comparison. Existing component ablations and the prior-effect visualization are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard deviations for MRI generation and across missing-modality configurations. v3 extends the existing reporting format to an additional comparator but introduces no seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Most matched numerical results remain unchanged, including PUIR's AutoPET Dice of 48.20. Added results include SwinMM/PCRL v2/VoCo Dice scores of 44.2/41.9/46.3, BRATS18 SwinUNETR pre-training scores, and 192-cube generation PSNR of 33.7418. Comparator removals delete corresponding results; these changes do not represent improved performance of the retained model under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: v3 adds Section 3.3, including Theorem 3.2's domain-adaptation risk bound, a patient/modality divergence decomposition in Equation 10, and a KL-based generalization comparison. v1 contains the representation hypothesis and loss formulations but no corresponding risk-bound analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim population-stable mappings from biological profiles to modalities and theoretical support for personalization's superior generalizability and transferability. This substantially strengthens v1's primarily empirical contribution claims, while retaining its broad application claims.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets pre-training as reducing conditional modality divergence and fine-tuning as reducing the patient-domain gap. It also interprets representation alignment as evidence for tighter generalization bounds. These extend the earlier information-completion explanation; the requirement for instance-matched modalities and associated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 promises future release of code, checkpoints, and data splits; v3 supplies a repository address and reports code and data-split availability. It also identifies the CFFF computing platform. Core pseudocode, hardware specifications, preprocessing, and training hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Ben-David's domain-adaptation theory, Cho's distribution-alignment work, SwinMM, and PCRLv2, extending its theoretical and SSL positioning. The existing related-work discussions are largely preserved. VoCo was already cited in v1, although its evaluated comparison is new.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten. Method sections are organized around pre-training and fine-tuning, experimental Sections 4–6 become Sections 4.1–4.3, and the appendices are reorganized. Imaging-principle descriptions move into a dedicated appendix.

P2.justification: v3 adds a patient/modality schematic, two t-SNE displays, and a qualitative close-up figure. Table 1 becomes three task panels, Table 2 becomes an aggregate summary with detailed results retained in the appendix, and the prior-effect figure and detailed AutoPET table move to the supplement.

improvement.justification: The added SSL controls, input-size check, clearer organization, and code-access information improve empirical assessment and usability. However, v3 elevates theoretical superiority to a core claim while Section 3.3 leaves its divergence decomposition and KL identities unestablished; the appended t-SNE evidence does not resolve those gaps. These substantive benefits and concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
